thread:
jonathan: Heads-up — OTEL collector in us-west-2 is showing sustained inflight queue spikes from gpu-node pool, and we've lost ~10-20% of runtime spans in the last 20m. Logs show repeated `processor/backpressure: queue full, rejecting` entries.

maria: ugh. any obvious network errors at the node level or just collector slowdowns?

jonathan: Seems correlated with a burst of profiling/tracing from a canary job — lots of large span payloads (kv cache dumps). Also we see NIC TX drops on the hosts: `TX packets: dropped` in dmesg.

wei: can you paste the collector backpressure lines?

jonathan: ```
2026-03-18T14:02:11Z INFO processor/backpressure queue full capacity=500 in_flight=512 rejecting=true
2026-03-18T14:02:12Z WARN exporter/otlp failed to export: context deadline exceeded
2026-03-18T14:02:13Z INFO receiver/trace accepted=120 dropped=18
```

tara: that capacity=500 is our per-instance pipeline queue right? if workload suddenly sends batched large spans we'll blow it. We can either increase queue, shard collectors, or throttle the agent side.

maria: short term, can we bump collector concurrency and export retries? also tail-sampling could reduce volume — but need to be careful with heat/latency.

jonathan: tried scaling collectors up (x2) — inflight improved but host NIC still shows tx drops. suspect GRO/LRO offload or kernel ring saturation under high packet per second.

wei: test commands to run on host: `ss -s`, `ethtool -S eth0 | grep tx_`, `cat /proc/net/softnet_stat` and tcpdump to confirm packet sizes. Also check if iptables conntrack is spiking.

tara: noted. I'll run quick checks on two impacted nodes. If rings are full we could enable larger tx ring with `ethtool -G eth0 tx 4096` (do one node at a time). Add to runbook if it helps.

maria: longer term: instrument the SDKs to prefer smaller span batch sizes for profiler spans; add an ingest-side size limit to drop/trim huge spans and emit a metric we can alert on.

jonathan: agreed. Also thinking about adding a collector-level rate limiter for spans by resource (gpu-host) and a dedicated trace pipeline for profiling spans that routes to a low-priority exporter (or S3) instead of OTLP stream.

infra-oncall: FYI, autoscaler handled collector pod increase but we had pod restarts because of oom in the exporter worker. Might need memory bump too.

maria: we'll need dashboard panels: collector inflight queue, exporter latency, host TX drops, host softnet backlog, and per-resource span size distribution. I'll add tickets.

wei: alert tuning idea: existing `otel-collector-inflight > 400` fires too often during short bursts. Replace with `avg_over_time(inflight[5m]) > 350 and max_over_time(dropped[5m]) > 5` to reduce noise and focus on real backpressure.

jonathan: good call. Also add an alert for `node_softnet_backlog > 1000` and tie to runbook that suggests ring size increase and ethtool checks.

tara: quick mitigation plan I can run now: 1) throttle profiler canary (scale down) 2) restart collector exporter worker with increased MEM limit 3) run ethtool ring bump on one node 4) enable temporary tail-sampling config to drop low-value spans. Want me to execute?

jonathan: do it. I'll coordinate with infra-oncall for the kernel ring change window. mark as P0 until we see drops stop.

sre-bot: Incident created: INCIDENT-2026-147 otel-ingest-backpressure-us-west (severity: P1) — assigned to eng-sre.

maria: after immediate steps, let's schedule an infra/agent working session next week to: - harden collector configs for high-latency exporters - define a profiling span size limit - add per-tenant rate limiting and fallback export path - update dashboards + alert rules

jonathan: thanks. I'll push a tiny PR to the runbook with the ethtool commands and the alert rule suggestions.

infra-oncall: done with the ring bump and exporter restart on node gpu-12, inflight queue dropped from ~480 -> ~80, dropped spans 0 for last 3m. monitoring looks stable.

maria: :thumbsup: let's keep this open for 1 hour after stabilization then close the incident if clean.

jonathan: closing note: action items assigned to maria/wei/tara. I'll file the follow-ups.
